ai_summary: Great Britain is currently generating 12.2 GW of wind power, with Scotland contributing an estimated 1.5 GW, representing 14.9% of its installed wind capacity. This clean dispatch underscores a stark regional contrast in grid decarbonisation, with Scottish carbon intensity sitting at 0 gCO2/kWh compared to 61 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, severe cross-border transmission limits continue to strand zero-carbon power north of the border. So far today, 6,735 MWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed through the Balancing Mechanism at a direct constraint cost of about £395,226. To plug this localized deficit, thermal plant output had to be procured downstream, resulting in an estimated 1,279,707 m3 of gas burned elsewhere and adding 2,357 tonnes of CO2 to the atmosphere. Extrapolating today’s constraint spend yields an estimated yearly curtailment cost of £144 million. When socialised through policy and balancing charges across total national demand, this ongoing constraint expense adds an estimated £0.5/MWh to electricity invoices across the UK, underscoring the urgent economic and environmental imperative to reinforce grid infrastructure.
